section_summary: This section details efforts by the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) and the Japanese Government during 1949 to increase Japan's coal production to a target of 42 million metric tons without deficit financing or price hikes. It includes diplomatic despatches, press releases, SCAP directives (notably SCAPIN 1984), and newspaper editorials addressing industry rationalization, labor issues, wage arrears, housing, and mine mechanization. Additionally, the documents cover visits and surveys by American mining consultants, a Japanese coal mission to the United States, geological assessments of coal exploration by Dr. Raymond C. Moore, and State Department research on indigenous metallurgical coking coal.

subfiles.about: Transmits a report and enclosures on SCAP's drive to expand Japanese coal production to 42 million tons for fiscal year 1949-50 without price increases or subsidies.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 207 details the Economic and Scientific Section's campaign to rationalize Japan's coal mining industry and achieve a 42-million-ton production goal for the 1949-50 fiscal year. The report outlines measures to eliminate abuses including wage non-payment, fictitious overtime, and excessive surface staffing, while reforming accounting and curbing unneeded stockpiling. It also discusses U.S. technical assistance, visits by American coal consultants, and Japanese reactions reported in the press and official boards.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 207: Drive for Increased Japanese Coal Production

subfiles.about: Announces the 42-million-ton coal production target for the 1949 Japanese fiscal year and the arrival of American consulting engineer Richard H. Barry.
subfiles.from: M. A. Wyatt, Coal Coordinator, ESS/Industry, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Wyatt announces the 42-million-ton coal production goal for the 1949 fiscal year, requiring increased worker efficiency. He notes SCAP assistance, including the arrival of American coal consultant Richard H. Barry to modernize operations in Kyushu.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 207: Press Statement by M. A. Wyatt, Coal Coordinator, ESS/Industry

subfiles.about: Directs the Japanese Government to implement measures stabilizing the coal industry to produce 42 million tons without price increases, subsidies, or deficit financing.
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy, Colonel, AGD, Adjutant General, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: SCAP instructs the Japanese Government to ensure prompt wage payments, end fictitious overtime, enforce a 60-40 underground-to-surface worker ratio, prioritize operating supplies, and establish uniform accounting.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 207: SCAPIN 1984, Memorandum for Japanese Government: Stabilization of the Coal Industry

subfiles.about: Publicizes SCAP's directive ordering the Japanese Government to correct malpractices and improve efficiency in the coal industry to reach the 42-million-ton quota.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, GHQ Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the SCAP directive ordering the Japanese Government to correct coal industry abuses, eliminate unpaid wages and unwarranted overtime, restrict surface hiring, and use blocked bank accounts if needed.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 207: Press Release: Correction of Coal Industry Urged

subfiles.about: Criticizes coal industry malpractices and explains SCAP assistance, including consultants Richard H. Barry and Paul R. Paulick, to meet the 1949 production quota.
subfiles.from: M. A. Wyatt, Coal Coordinator, ESS/Industry, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Wyatt rebukes operators for financial delinquencies and inflated costs, explains SCAPIN 1984, and outlines U.S. assistance, including consultants Richard H. Barry in Kyushu, Paul R. Paulick in Hokkaido, machinery imports, and engineering missions.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 4 to Despatch No. 207: Press Statement by M. A. Wyatt, Coal Coordinator, ESS/Industry

subfiles.about: Examines the severe financial distress, unpaid accounts, and need for rationalization facing the Japanese coal industry under the Nine-Point Economic Stabilization Program.
subfiles.summary: An Osaka Mainichi editorial discusses mounting debts, tax arrears, and red-ink operations among coal mines, urging rationalization and improved distribution rather than taxpayer subsidies under the Nine-Point Economic Stabilization Program.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 5 to Despatch No. 207: Editorial: The Coal Industry and 9-Point Program

subfiles.about: Critiques coal industry complaints regarding SCAP's 42-million-ton goal and argues that eliminating waste, strikes, and corruption will make profitable production possible.
subfiles.summary: A Nippon Times editorial argues that despite industry complaints about production costs exceeding official prices, eliminating strikes, go-slow tactics, excessive office staff, and political slush funds can enable the coal industry to break even.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 6 to Despatch No. 207: Editorial: The Demand on the Coal Industry

subfiles.about: Reports on activities of American mining consultants, deliberations of the Coal Production Committee, and proposed reductions in coal mine housing loans.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports on Coal Production Committee meetings rejecting wage reductions below SCAPIN 1984 standards, pruning mine housing loan applications to 500 million yen, and transmitting a press release on American mining consultants' initial findings.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 272: Supplementary Information on Drive for Increased Coal Production in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports findings by American consultants Richard H. Barry and Paul R. Paulick showing that mechanization and labor adjustments can make Japanese mines profitable.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, GHQ Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Consultants Paulick and Barry report that Japanese coal mines can operate profitably at current prices through mechanization, shifting workers to face operations, modern haulage, and overcoming outmoded customs like carrying coal in baskets.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 272: Press Release: Experts Foresee Profitable Coal Mining Operations

subfiles.about: Transmits text of a press release announcing a 10-week tour of U.S. coal facilities by SCAP Coal Coordinator M. A. Wyatt and six Japanese mining experts.
subfiles.summary: Quotes a press release detailing a 10-week study tour to U.S. mines and machinery plants by SCAP Coal Coordinator Wyatt and six Japanese experts, including labor representatives Sadao Terachi and Eiji Nishijima, and industry officials.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-124: Wyatt and Six Coal Experts to Leave for U.S.

subfiles.about: Transmits GHQ Far East Command Information Bulletin No. 5 reviewing the coal mining industry from the surrender to the present.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits a GHQ Far East Command press release reviewing Japan's coal mining industry and postwar rehabilitation efforts.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 401: Statement on Japanese Coal Mining Industry

subfiles.about: Provides a comprehensive historical review of the Japanese coal industry from postwar collapse through rehabilitation programs and 1949 production objectives.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, GHQ Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Reviews postwar conditions in Japanese coal mines, labor recruitment, machinery manufacturing, housing construction, and financial deficits, outlining plans to achieve 42 million tons in fiscal year 1949 through mechanization and rationalization.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 401: Information Bulletin No. 5: The Coal Mining Industry

subfiles.about: Quotes a press release detailing recommendations by consulting geologist Dr. Raymond C. Moore regarding Japanese coal exploration, mining laws, and survey agencies.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a press release summarizing Dr. Raymond C. Moore's recommendations to revise mining laws, eliminate exploration subsidies, strengthen the Geological Survey, standardize reserve computations, and send Japanese geologists to the United States.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-250: Moore Reports on Coal Exploration

subfiles.about: Requests an expert evaluation of Caleb Davies's report suggesting Japan could become self-sufficient in metallurgical coking coal through beneficiation.
subfiles.from: Warren S. Hunsberger, Acting Chief, Division of Research for Far East, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Requests Bureau of Mines evaluation of Caleb Davies's report proposing Japanese self-sufficiency in metallurgical coking coal.
subfiles.title: Letter: Inquiries Regarding Caleb Davies's Report on Metallurgical Coking Coal in Japan
subfiles.to: A. C. Fieldner, Chief, Fuels and Explosives Division, Bureau of Mines, Department of the Interior

subfiles.about: Thanks Dr. Fieldner for his comments, citations, and enclosure regarding metallurgical coke production in Japan.
subfiles.from: Warren S. Hunsberger, Acting Chief, Division of Research for Far East, Department of State
keywords: Division of Research for Far East
subfiles.summary: Thanks A. C. Fieldner for comments, citations, and materials regarding Japanese metallurgical coke production.
subfiles.title: Letter: Acknowledgment of Comments on Metallurgical Coke Production in Japan
subfiles.to: A. C. Fieldner, Chief, Fuels and Explosives Division, Bureau of Mines, Department of the Interior
